chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The offering of condolences is [performed] to the bereaved after the burial.

key_terms.أَهْلِ الْمُصِيبَةِ: The people of the calamity (the bereaved family)
key_terms.التَّعْزِيَةُ: Condolences or comfort offered to the bereaved

ai.seo_question: When should one offer condolences after a death in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the specific timing for ta'ziyah, distinguishing it from the immediate mourning period by mandating that formal condolences occur after the burial (dafn). In Shia jurisprudence, this timing allows the bereaved family to complete the initial rites and rest, while ensuring the community's support arrives when the practical burdens of burial are lifted. This distinction highlights the structured nature of grief in Islamic tradition, balancing emotional support with ritual completion.
